1.0.2: Each and JoinEach use new UUID to pair messages.
1.1.0: JoinEach has optional Correlation ID properties.
Each has additional output port options - Correlation ID and Items Count
1.1.1: JoinEach does not attempt to read originalMessage.correlationId.
1.1.2: JoinEach works with 0 count, tooltips changed.
1.2.0: Each stores index into state while sending an array to the output port. Prevents duplicates in case of crash.
1.3.0: Each generates output variables based on the input variables schema.
1.4.0: Change default label for variable properties.
1.4.2: Restore Index and Value variables to Each component along with property variables.
1.4.3: Fix variables output for Each component when the used field has no schema.
1.4.4: Fix Each connector causing an issue that would make the engine unresponsive in certain flow designs.
Each connector now can output properties from a nested property used as input.
1.8.0: Update Switch component to support same conditions as Condition component.
1.8.1: Fix Each component to handle transforms properly.
1.8.2: Fix SetVariable: Handles all types of variables.
1.8.3: Enhance OnError to handle large number of errors and added limit.
1.9.0: Added Digest utility to "pile up" entries until either a threshold is reached or a time interval is timed out at which point the Digest outputs all the entries as a batch.
1.9.1: Digest: set * as a default for hour, dayMonth, dayWeek and 0 for minute.
1.9.2: Digest: Set quotas to handle concurrent entries in a more robust way.
1.9.3: Digest: Tuned to handle higher number of concurrent entries.
1.9.4: OnError: fixing 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')'.
1.9.5: Digest: fixing 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'zone')'.
1.10.0: Implemented multiselect input normalization for Testing component multiselect fields.
1.11.0: Added component CodeBlock: Allows you to write JavaScript code to transform data.
1.12.0: Each: Added delay option to control timing between items.
1.12.1: Set Variable: do not provide 'undefined' variable to the output.
1.12.2: Fix an issue with missing dependencies for `Condition` and `Switch` components that caused them to not work in some environments.
1.12.3: Fix missing properties in the schema for `Testing` component.
1.12.4: Each: reject negative delay (prevented an infinite timeout loop), persist the absolute index on resume to avoid duplicate items, and minor cleanups.
1.12.5: Each: add output examples for 'Items Count' and 'Correlation ID', and mark the item dropdown source as not requiring auth.
1.12.6: Each: make the delayed loop resumable so the engine's automatic message re-delivery (on a transient error such as a dropped keep-alive connection surfacing as EPROTO) continues from the persisted index instead of restarting from item 0; use the retry-stable, per-execution context id as the Each<->JoinEach correlation ID instead of a generated UUID, so it stays identical across a re-delivery (keeps pairing intact) without depending on persisted state; skip the plugin store entirely when all items fit the first batch; reject a non-numeric or negative delay (a transform could otherwise feed a value that yields a NaN batch size) and always clamp the batch size to a finite value of at least 1 to prevent a stuck loop when the configured timeout interval is smaller than the delay.
1.13.0: Added test() (Flow Test Mode) to triggers (OnError, OnStart).
1.14.0: Each: added the 'Sequential' option. The next item is sent only after the previous one has been confirmed by the new 'Continue Each' component, so the items keep their order even when the steps in the loop take a varying amount of time. An item that is not confirmed within 'Item Timeout' is skipped over, so the loop cannot hang.

Each: the 'done' port has a new 'Result' output - one entry per item of a sequential loop, in item order: the named fields that 'Continue Each' added for that item, or null for an item skipped after 'Item Timeout'.
Added component Continue Each: ends one pass of a sequential Each loop and can add named values ('Add to Result' rows of Name + Value) from the loop body to the 'Result' of Each.
1.14.1: Condition: 'Contains' and 'Regex' no longer throw 'Cannot read properties of undefined' on a null/undefined input (e.g. an empty field from the previous component); such an input now routes to the 'false' port instead of being retried and stored as unprocessed. An invalid regular expression is now a non-retryable error.
1.14.2: Condition: every clause must have a supported operator. The input schema now requires 'operator' (one of the supported operators) on each clause, so flow validation reports a clause without one, by its position, and the designer highlights the Operator select of that clause. The Copilot runs that validation after it saves a flow; saving or starting a flow without validation still accepts such a clause. At runtime, a message that reaches such a clause is no longer cancelled with 'Unsupported operator: undefined'. It fails input validation (e.g. '/expression/AND/0/OR/1 must have required property operator') and is kept as an unprocessed message. A flow whose Condition input has a top-level field other than 'expression' no longer starts.
1.14.3: Switch: 'Contains' and 'Regex' no longer throw 'Cannot read properties of undefined' on a null/undefined input (e.g. a field missing from the previous component's output); such a clause now evaluates to false, so the message goes to the next matching output or to 'else' instead of being retried and stored as unprocessed. A null input is no longer compared as the text 'null'. An invalid regular expression is now a non-retryable error. Same behaviour as Condition since 1.14.1.
1.14.4: Digest: 'Drain by Schedule' no longer stops with 'Parameter timeout should be less than 2678400000' when the next scheduled run is more than 31 days away (e.g. a monthly schedule across a DST change, or a day of month 29-31 crossing a shorter month). Long waits are split into chained timeouts of at most one day, and entries are drained only when the scheduled date is reached. An invalid schedule is now a non-retryable error.
1.14.5: Security: upgraded uuid to 11.1.1 (missing buffer bounds check in v3/v5/v6).
1.14.6: Security: upgraded lodash to 4.18.1 (prototype pollution in _.unset/_.omit, code injection in _.template).
1.14.7: Each: no longer keeps a continuity scope for 100 days for every message. Each declares a webhook (Continue Each wakes a sequential loop through it), so the engine stores a continuity scope for every message into Each, and that scope keeps the message scopes it refers to from being garbage collected. Only a sequential loop reads it. Each now sets its lifetime with context.setMaxWait(): a parallel or delayed loop (and an empty, invalid or rejected input) lets it go at once, a sequential loop keeps it until the loop can be over at the latest (items x (Item Timeout + Delay), plus one hour). Takes effect on engines where setMaxWait() can shorten the lifetime; older engines keep the 100-day default and work as before.
1.14.8: Each (sequential): many loops running at once on one Each no longer slow down the whole tenant. The list and the progress of every running loop were kept in the component state of Each, which the engine stores as one document per component and reads in full for every message, so with many concurrent loops each item cost the workers megabytes of parsing. They are now kept in the flow state, one entry per loop. Loops started by the previous version continue: they are moved to the flow state when their next item is confirmed or times out.

JoinEach: the same fix. The messages collected by every join in progress were kept in the component state of JoinEach (one document per component, read in full for every message), so many joins in progress at once - or joins that never complete and stay behind - slowed down every message of the component and could hit the 16 MB document limit. They are now kept in the flow state, one entry per join. Joins started by the previous version continue: they are moved to the flow state by their next message or timeout.

Continue Each: when many sequential loops confirm their items at the same moment, the confirmation could be rejected by the hosted API gateway ('max connections reached', HTTP 429) or by a full input queue (HTTP 503) and the message failed, leaving the item to wait for the engine retry or the Item Timeout. Such a momentary rejection is now retried a few times with a short random backoff (about 20 seconds at most).

Each (sequential): a confirmation that arrived while Each was still recording the item it had just sent (a fast loop body, a busy worker) could be taken as a late one and ignored, so the item waited for the Item Timeout and its Result entry became null. Confirmations are now always checked against the recorded item under the loop lock.

Each (sequential): the number of loops one Each may run at the same time can be limited with the connector configuration 'sequentialEachMaxConcurrentLoops' (service appmixer:utils:controls, a positive integer; not set = no limit). A loop over the limit is not started: the message fails with an error that is logged and retried by the engine, so the loop starts once another loop on that Each is over.
